title: Fundamental Rights — State (Art. 12) and Laws Inconsistent with Fundamental Rights (Art. 13)

content.overview: Article 12 defines the State for Part III, unless the context otherwise requires, as the Government and Parliament of India, the Government and the Legislature of each State, and all local or other authorities within the territory of India or under the control of the Government of India. Article 13 provides that laws inconsistent with Part III are void to the extent of the inconsistency. It covers pre-constitutional and post-constitutional laws. Law includes any ordinance, order, bye-law, rule, regulation, notification, and custom or usage having the force of law. A constitutional amendment is dealt with in Article 13(4) and Article 368, and that interaction stays on the case-law gate.

sections.heading: Article 12 — State
sections.body: Article 12 defines the State for Part III purposes: Government and Parliament of India, Government and Legislature of each State, and all local or other authorities within the territory of India or under the control of the Government of India.

sections.heading: Article 13 — Inconsistent laws
sections.body: Article 13 addresses pre-Constitution and post-Constitution laws inconsistent with Part III, including the prohibition on State making laws that take away or abridge fundamental rights, void to the extent of contravention.

learningObjectives: State the Article 13 inconsistency rule and the definition of law.
Keep constitutional-amendment review on the case-law gate.
enhancement.definition: Article 12 identifies the State bound by Part III. Article 13 makes inconsistent laws void to the extent of the inconsistency.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: State-only rights do not run against a person outside Article 12. Article 13 is a consequence rule, not a separate fundamental right.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Constitution of India, Articles 12 and 13. Article 13(4) says Article 13 does not apply to an amendment under Article 368; the basic-structure challenge to that position is not restated as a holding.
essentialIngredients: Instrument identified as government, legislature, local authority or other authority
Control of the Government of India if the body is outside the territory
Inconsistency with a specific Part III right
Void only to the extent of inconsistency
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Article 12 has four limbs: Union Government and Parliament, State Government and Legislature, local authorities, and other authorities within India or under the control of the Government of India. A private club or company is not the State merely because it is regulated. Other-authority doctrine is case-law and is not given a test here. Article 13(1) deals with pre-constitutional laws and Article 13(2) with laws made after commencement. The voidness is pro tanto. The definition of law is wider than a statute. Article 13(4) excludes Article 368 amendments from Article 13; whether that exclusion is itself limited is a case-law question and is flagged.
examples: A municipal bye-law excludes a citizen from a public well on a forbidden ground. The municipality is a local authority and the bye-law is law under Article 13.
A private landlord refuses a tenant. Article 12 is not met for an Article 14 claim.
An Act is inconsistent with Article 14 in one proviso only. Article 13 voids that inconsistency, not the whole Act by default.
enhancement.problemApplication: Classify the respondent under Article 12. If the challenge is to a norm, test the Article 13 definition. Then name the Part III article breached.
distinctions: Article 12 State vs a private person
Article 13 law vs a constitutional amendment
Pro tanto voidness vs striking down an entire statute
enhancement.caseLawNotes: No new case citation or ratio was added. Names already in the published overview are not promoted to verified holdings.
enhancement.shortAnswerStructure: Article 12 defines the State. Article 13 voids inconsistent laws to the extent of the inconsistency.
enhancement.tenMarkStructure: Article 12 limbs → Article 13 pre- and post-constitutional laws → definition of law → amendment flag.
enhancement.sixteenMarkStructure: Why these two articles frame Part III → State → law → extent of voidness → what is not decided here → facts → conclusion.

keyTakeaways: Article 12 lists government, legislature, local and other authorities.
Most Part III rights need that State.
Article 13 voids inconsistent law only to the extent of inconsistency.
Law includes custom having the force of law.
Article 368 interaction is a case-law gate.

verification.note: Text of Articles 12 and 13. Other-authority and basic-structure tests not invented.

content.study: Decide Article 12 before applying a State-only right. Use Article 13 only against a law as defined. Do not call every private body a State without the local or other authority test.
